name: Kaapa
subtitle: garhwali spinach thickened with gram flour, garlicky and eaten by the bowl with rice

ingredients.note: the thickener. No cream or dairy goes into kaapa
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free

prepNotes: Wash the spinach in three changes of water. Hill spinach comes in gritty and grit in kaapa is unforgiveable.
Whisk the besan into 200ml cold water until completely smooth before you start cooking, and leave it aside. Lumps will not come out later.
Blanch and blend the spinach only if you want it smooth; many Garhwali homes leave it coarse and chopped.

steps.text: Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 90 seconds, drain and plunge into cold water to fix the colour.
steps.tip: Ninety seconds, no more. Overcooked spinach goes olive and dull.

steps.text: Squeeze out the excess water and either chop it fine or pulse it briefly in a blender to a coarse puree.
Heat the mustard oil until it smokes, cut the flame for a minute, then crackle the cumin and fenugreek seeds for 20 seconds.
steps.tip: Fenugreek turns bitter quickly. The moment it reddens, move on.

steps.text: Add the hing, red chillies, garlic, ginger and green chillies and fry 2 minutes until the garlic is golden.
Stir in the turmeric and coriander powder, then pour in the smooth besan slurry, whisking continuously.
Cook the besan mixture on a low flame for 6-8 minutes until it thickens and stops smelling of raw flour.
steps.tip: Raw besan is the single most common fault in kaapa. Give it the full 8 minutes.

steps.text: Add the spinach, the remaining 200ml water and salt. Simmer uncovered 10 minutes until it is thick enough to hold a ridge from the spoon.
Finish with the lemon juice off the heat and serve with hot rice.

storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat gently with a splash of water; the colour dulls on day two but the flavour improves.
